newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end pit trading weaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end pit trading weaker.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended pit trading moderately lower as the market adjusted from Wednesday's surge and braced for Friday's U.S. labor figures.
December Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures corrected a small portion of Wednesday's rally in trade that lacked followthrough in either direction on Thursday.
Nearby S&Ps probed above Wednesday's all-time high at 700.00 by a couple of ticks early on Thursday, stalled and then explored the downside but also lacked extension.
"We had a minor correction in bonds and stocks...but there was a lack of followthrough," said a S&P 500 floor analyst.
Futures generally respected ranges during the afternoon, when T-bond futures had shaken off light pressure and finished barely changed before the jobs data.
September nonfarm payrolls on average are forecast rising 166,000, with the jobless rate seen slipping to 5.2 percent and average hourly earnings expected to rise 0.2 percent.
In August, payrolls grew by 250,000, unemployment fell to 5.1 percent, the lowest since 5.0 percent in March 1989, and hourly earnings increased 0.5 percent to $11.87 from $11.81.
Trading flows dwindled from Thursday's, with closing action called "dead, a nonevent" by another S&P 500 floor broker.

Some traders said the contract still appears to have more upside ultimately, although whether it will correct further on the downside first could depend on the payrolls figures and the reaction of U.S. Treasury bond futures.
"In the worst-case scenario, if it (payrolls) comes in higher than expected, then we'll have a breakoff...but the way it looked today, it looks more and more supported," said a third floor broker.
December S&P 500s approached but stayed above the top of a downside chart gap that starts at 696.25, Wednesday's IMM low, and extends down to 695.30, Tuesday's overall high.
December Nikkei 225 futures fell on sales from four large firms that one broker said looked like new selling and which offset one dealer's morning purchases of about 800 contracts.
"I think the guy just wants to be short," the broker said of one house's sales. "It's new shorts coming in." But the contract stayed range-bound between 21,000.0 and 21,600.0.
Futures ignored a 1.9-percent drop in August U.S. factory orders. Traders had expected a 1.2-percent fall.

Dec S&P 500s settled down 1.65 pts at 697.70, Value Lines lost 1.85 to 646.45, Nikkei fell 295.0 to 21,300.0, and NYSE Composite fell 0.65 to 372.70. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
